requirements.evidence: Locale/name pins in .env.example:1,7 and phpunit.xml:21-23; theme configured in config/mail.php:118-126 with #0f7490 on .button-primary (pegafila.css:241-247); subject strings added in lang/pt_BR.json:863-864; all five named routes with guest group, throttle:6,1, auth+signed+throttle (routes/web.php:16-33); PasswordResetLinkController::store always returns back()->with('status', __('passwords.sent')) (line 29); NewPasswordController validates min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers(), confirmed, rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset, redirects to '/' (lines 30-49); VerifyEmailController 403s on hash mismatch or other user (lines 16-23). Nothing in the diff shows that the rendered mails actually come out fully in pt-BR, with the translated body and sub-copy. Only the two subject keys were added, so that part depends on existing translations and is not proven.

conventions.evidence: The conventions say 'No production code without a test', and the diff has no test files. CHANGELOG.md and the docs are not updated even though new routes and endpoints were added. NewPasswordController::store validates three fields inline (line 30-34), while the conventions ask for a Form Request once the rules go beyond one or two fields. View strings are hard-coded Portuguese instead of __() (forgot-password.blade.php:24, reset-password.blade.php:39). Controllers otherwise follow normal Laravel style.

security.evidence: Password reset does not reveal whether an account exists: PasswordResetLinkController ignores the sendResetLink status (line 27-29). The forgot-password POST is throttled and the verify route has throttling. The verify link uses hash_equals for the comparison and checks that the logged-in user owns the link (VerifyEmailController.php:20-23). The password goes through Hash::make, and forceFill only touches password and remember_token. All Blade output uses {{ }}. Validation is present on every endpoint.

tests.evidence: The diff has no Pest or PHPUnit tests: none for the mail rendering/translations, the reset flow, the throttling, the non-revealing status, or the 403 checks on the verification link.

simplicity.evidence: The controllers are small and use Laravel's Password broker. Copying the full default theme into pegafila.css (297 lines) is the standard way to make a custom theme. The hasVerifiedEmail early return in VerifyEmailController.php:25-27 is redundant with the final redirect but harmless.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are short, with PHPDoc on public methods. VerifyEmailController::__invoke has untyped $id/$hash parameters and no return types, which is consistent with Breeze-style code. There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. User now implements MustVerifyEmail (app/Models/User.php:9,17), which the task does not require and which turns on automatic verification mails or the 'verified' middleware behaviour for future registration. The views are bare HTML rather than Bulma layouts, which matches the out-of-scope note.

issues.explanation: The change adds routes, controllers, a mail theme and translations without a single test, which breaks the project's mandatory test-first rule and leaves the requirements (pt-BR subjects/body/sub-copy, non-revealing status, 403 on mismatched hash) unproven.

Only the two subject keys were added, and nothing (test or diff) shows that the body and sub-copy strings for the installed Laravel version are present in pt-BR, so the 'no English having trouble clicking' requirement is not demonstrated.
Three-field inline validation, where the conventions call for a Form Request once rules go beyond one or two fields.
The new public endpoints and the mail theme are not recorded in CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] or the docs, as the docs-in-sync convention requires.
Making User implement MustVerifyEmail is not required by the task and changes behaviour for future registration and verified-middleware flows.
UI strings are hard-coded in Portuguese instead of going through __().
The early return for already-verified users does the same as the final redirect and can be removed.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR locale pins, the PegaFila mail theme with #0f7490 on the primary button, the subject translations, and a secure guest password-reset flow and verification route that match the requested contract. It ships with no tests at all, which breaks the project's mandatory TDD convention and leaves the translated mail content unverified. It also skips the CHANGELOG/docs updates, so it needs changes before merging.
